title: Cross Lingual Transfer in Tulu Legal Comprehension: Script-Dependent Improvement and RAG-Induced Knowledge Conflict
abstract: arXiv:2608.28645v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Low-resource languages without an adequate training corpus often use a related, higher-resource language as a scaffold for comprehension. Still, there is a need to develop rigorous evaluation methods to identify when models fail in cross lingual low-resource environments. Using the legal domain as a backdrop, three models (Llama3, Hex-1, Sarvam) were tested on the ability to classify legal complaints written in a low resource Dravidian language (Tulu). Transliterating queries across Dravidian scripts allowed models to gain a preliminary understanding of speakers' complaints without the use of wide scale training, though the level of comprehension was heavily script dependent (with Kannada - another relatively low-resource language - producing the strongest positive trend). translated_title: 图鲁语法律理解中的跨语言迁移：依赖文字系统的提升与RAG引发的知识冲突
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.28645v1 公告类型：cross 摘要：缺乏足够训练语料的低资源语言，通常使用一种相关的、资源更丰富的语言作为理解的辅助框架。尽管如此，仍然需要开发严格的评估方法，以识别模型在跨语言低资源环境中何时会失败。以法律领域为背景，本研究测试了三个模型（Llama3、Hex-1、Sarvam）对以低资源达罗毗荼语言（图鲁语）书写的法律投诉进行分类的能力。在达罗毗荼文字系统之间对查询进行音译转写，使模型无需大规模训练即可对说话者的投诉获得初步理解，尽管理解程度高度依赖于所使用的文字系统（其中卡纳达语——另一种相对低资源的语言——产生了最强的积极趋势）。在RAG框架下从卡纳达语法律文件语料库中进行检索，结果好坏参半：某些模型在特定条件下对理解表现出微弱的积极趋势。
tldr: 本研究通过跨文字音译与RAG检索评估三个大模型对低资源达罗毗荼语言图鲁语法律投诉的分类理解能力，发现跨文字迁移带来的理解提升高度依赖目标文字系统（卡纳达语效果最佳），而RAG检索可能引发知识冲突导致效果好坏参半。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates three LLMs on classifying legal complaints in low-resource Tulu via cross-script transliteration and RAG, revealing that comprehension gains are heavily script-dependent (with Kannada transliteration yielding the strongest improvement) while RAG retrieval induces knowledge conflicts with mixed results.
